verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. As a formula in the symbols B, σ, u, L, K, g the Lean definition is the display verbatim: representativeFrequency B σ u L K g = B • (K − (σu/(L‖g‖²)) • g), with g = shearVector F0 G0 q0 = (R·F_R, G_R) in the paper's (θ, z) order, and FamilyData.frequency_identity states the left-hand side as the paper writes it, (target/R0, pz) = frequency, where target = R0·(frequency)_0 is the paper's p̃ and pz = (frequency)_1. The one difference is the value fed in for K. The construction (PrimaryGeometryAssembly.family, also BasePhaseGeometry.Representatives.family) sets K := transverseDirection g = −quarterTurn(N) = (N_z, −N_θ), while the paper says K = (−N_z, N_θ) = quarterTurn(N). So K_lean = −K_paper, and by algebra the Lean vector at sign σ is minus the paper's vector at sign −σ: B(−K_p − (σu/(L|g|²))g) = −B(K_p − ((−σ)u/(L|g|²))g). Both signs are constructed (family is indexed by c : Fin 2 with phaseSign c = ±1), so each formula is obtained from the other by unfolding transverseDirection, substituting σ ↦ −σ and negating; no analytic fact is involved. The convention is used consistently in the repository: Lean's frame relation is quarterTurn K = N (quarterTurn_transverseDirection, FamilyData.eigen12/eigen21), whereas the paper's (7.7) has N_a = ((K_a)_z, −(K_a)_θ) = −quarterTurn K_a; under n ↦ −n, σ ↦ −σ these agree, and the radial component B·s(v) and the slope ⟪frequency, g⟫ = −σBu/L (representative_slope) have the paper's values for the same σ. Not verified here: that the downstream wave sum is invariant under Φ ↦ −Φ (the paper sums e^{ikmΦ} over m ∈ ℤ∖{0}, which suggests it, but I did not trace the Lean wave field), and that nothing else in the label depends on σ in a way that breaks the relabelling. The rounding of k·p̃ (Lean: floor with 0 replaced by 1; paper: nearest nonzero integer) is the prose after the display and is not part of this block.
